title: Section 8 Landlords in Shaker Heights: High Standards, High Rents, Inspection Culture
metaTitle: Section 8 Landlord Shaker Heights: Rent, Paperwork
metaDescription: Section 8 landlord Shaker Heights guide: CMHA's 17-suburb occupancy paperwork, ZIP-code payment standards, the rent reasonableness test and the 40% rule.
secondaryKeywords: section 8 large house bedroom size cmha
answerBox: Shaker Heights is one of 17 suburbs where CMHA collects a Certificate of Occupancy and/or Rental Registration with the Request for Tenancy Approval. CMHA sets the subsidy ceiling by ZIP code rather than by city, and approves your rent through a reasonableness test measured against comparable unassisted units and applied to gross rent.

sections.h2: Shaker Heights is on CMHA's 17-suburb list
body: CMHA licenses nobody: **"CMHA does not have a pre-approval process for landlords or units."** The gate is municipal. Shaker Heights is one of **17 named suburbs** where CMHA collects a **Certificate of Occupancy and/or Rental Registration with the Request for Tenancy Approval**, so the city document has to exist before the RFTA goes in.

It is asked for twice: CMHA pays a new contract on the next scheduled payment date after it receives the signed contracts, the executed lease and the **"occupancy permit, when applicable"** — payment dates are generally the **3rd and 16th**. We do not print the city's fees or renewal cadence here; stale figures are how owners under-budget a lease-up.

sections.h2: The ceiling follows the ZIP code, not the city line
body: CMHA implemented **Small Area Fair Market Rent** standards effective January 1, 2025, so the ceiling attaches to the ZIP. Its Rent Determination tool publishes FY2026 figures effective **January 1, 2026** for **53 ZIP codes**; countywide the two-bedroom standard runs from **$1,096 in ZIP 44127 to $2,169 in ZIPs 44113 and 44040**. Below are adjacent ZIPs in this part of the county. Boundaries do not follow municipal lines, so look the address up; there is no static PDF, and the tool is revised annually. [Payment standards by ZIP](/cmha-payment-standards-by-zip-code/) maps the rest.

sections.h2: A high ceiling is not an approved rent
body: **"The payment standard is NOT the maximum amount that the landlord can charge; it is the maximum amount of subsidy that the CMHA will pay toward each tenant's rent portion."** Your number is set instead by rent reasonableness, whose terms favor a well-kept property. Under **24 CFR 982.507(b)** the authority compares the unit to **other comparable unassisted units**, weighing location, quality, size, unit type and age, plus amenities, housing services, maintenance and utilities furnished under the lease — condition sits inside the test, and the benchmark is the unsubsidized market. Under **982.507(d)** every payment you accept certifies the rent is no more than you charge for comparable unassisted units in the premises. [Rent reasonableness](/cmha-rent-reasonableness-explained/) covers the determination.

The test runs on **gross rent**: rent plus tenant-paid utilities or the allowance. On a three-bedroom single-family unit where the tenant pays, CMHA's January 1, 2026 schedule allows **$71** gas space heat, **$81** other electricity, **$248** metered suburban water and sewer and **$16** suburban trash — all subtracted before your contract rent is set.

Plan on that first number standing: an increase needs a HAP contract a year old and a passed annual inspection, and on **August 14, 2025** CMHA asked Greater Cleveland landlords to forgo increases over a budget shortfall.

Two rules cap what a larger house earns. CMHA's Landlord Participation Guide states that a family selecting a unit **larger** than its voucher size gets the payment standard **and** utility allowance for the **smaller** of the two — a four-bedroom leased on a two-bedroom voucher is priced off the two-bedroom line. And on an **initial** contract the tenant's total portion paid to you may be **no more than 40% of monthly adjusted income**; above that, CMHA negotiates the rent down.

You cannot settle the difference privately: CMHA states that **"side deals between the landlord and family are illegal"** and can result in the family's termination and the landlord being disbarred or suspended. Check the voucher's bedroom size and **180-day** expiration early.

sections.h2: The inspection has no premium lane
body: A property in good condition gets the same visit as every other. CMHA's inspections run through **an outside firm** against the **13 key housing quality aspects**, and CMHA publishes no expedited, fast-track, pre-inspection or self-certification option. The standard is still HQS: the NSPIRE transition deadline **"has been moved from October 1, 2025 to February 1, 2027."**

What fails an otherwise solid unit is small and specifically dated. CMHA's 24-hour list runs to detectors, burners that will not ignite, no water, no heat between October 15 and April 15, sewer back-up and gas leak. Since **December 29, 2024** smoke detectors must sit on each level, inside each bedroom, within 21 feet of each bedroom door and in any living area separated by a door, hardwired or 10-year sealed; carbon monoxide detectors have been required since **December 27, 2022** with any gas appliance, attached garage or wood-burning fireplace.

Older stock carries one more clock: in a **pre-1978** unit cited for defective paint where a child under six will reside, you have **10 days from the initial inspection** to produce a passed clearance test and proof of certified abatement work. CMHA aims to inspect and notify **within 15 days** of RFTA submission and to **reinspect within five business days**, and may accept photographs rather than returning; initial inspections get **two attempts**.

sections.h2: Nobody in Shaker Heights can require you to do this
body: Ohio has no statewide source-of-income protection, and the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights' Ohio Advisory Committee states that **"[s]ource-of-income discrimination is legal in most of Ohio."** PRRAC's March 2026 compilation records five Cuyahoga County municipalities with local protections; **Shaker Heights is not among them.** That is a compilation rather than live ordinance text — confirm the code with the city and your counsel.

So the case has to be commercial, and stated honestly. CMHA's owner page advertises **"stable, guaranteed rent payments deposited directly into your account"** — CMHA's word, not ours. Its payment covers CMHA's share only, the tenant still owes theirs, and **"HCVP does not pay for tenant caused damages."** What is verifiable: over **15,000 voucher holders**, mandatory direct deposit, and screening that stays entirely yours.

We work Greater Cleveland and Cuyahoga County under CMHA, and **we have completed CMHA's Virtual Landlord Orientation** — required since **January 1, 2026** of the owner or managing agent, once every 24 months, before CMHA can execute a HAP contract for a new tenancy. Name us as agent and it is satisfied the day your RFTA is filed.

items: **Tenant placement — one month's rent**, charged only after the tenant is placed. No placement, no fee
**Inspection attendance and written report — $100.** Attend it yourself and pay nothing
**Management — 5% of monthly rent**, only while rented
**Repair estimates free and itemized inside 24 hours.** Nothing starts without your approval

body: Get the city's Certificate of Occupancy before the RFTA, price off the unit's own ZIP rather than a countywide figure, test that number against unassisted comparables on a gross-rent basis, and check the voucher's bedroom size first. Call **(440) 444-4737**, or read [Section 8 Stress Free](/section8stressfree).

faq.q: Do I need a Certificate of Occupancy to rent a Shaker Heights house to a voucher holder?
faq.a: Shaker Heights is one of 17 suburbs where CMHA collects a Certificate of Occupancy and/or Rental Registration when the RFTA is submitted, and it names an occupancy permit again in what it must receive before your first payment. That document comes from the city.

faq.q: What is CMHA's payment standard in Shaker Heights?
faq.a: It follows the ZIP code, not the city. Effective January 1, 2026, ZIP 44122 runs $1,514 studio to $2,858 four-bedroom while ZIP 44120 runs $994 to $1,875. Look the address up in CMHA's Rent Determination tool, which is revised annually.

faq.q: Can I charge more than the payment standard on a higher-end unit?
faq.a: CMHA is explicit that the payment standard is not the maximum a landlord may charge, only the maximum subsidy paid. The rent must still pass reasonableness against comparable unassisted units on a gross-rent basis, and on an initial contract the tenant's portion cannot exceed 40% of adjusted income.

faq.q: My house has four bedrooms but the family's voucher is for two. Which standard applies?
faq.a: The smaller one. CMHA's Landlord Participation Guide states that when a family selects a unit larger than the bedroom size on its voucher, CMHA applies the payment standard and the utility allowance for the smaller of the two. Check the voucher's size before you show a larger house.

faq.q: Does Shaker Heights require landlords to accept housing vouchers?
faq.a: Shaker Heights does not appear on PRRAC's March 2026 list of Cuyahoga County municipalities with source-of-income protections, and Ohio has no statewide protection. That is a compilation rather than live ordinance text, so confirm the current code with the city and your counsel.
